name: Signal and Consent: The BCI Rollout, 2091-2155
description: A rigorously researched historical documentary examining the sixty-four-year period of BCI normalization, from early voluntary adoption among Tier 4-5 populations through the economic incentive structures that made BCI integration effectively mandatory for Tier 1-2 workers seeking employment in the newly restructured labor markets. The film pays particular attention to the 2118 Neural Commons Agreement, presenting substantial archival evidence that the agreement's 'informed consent' provisions were written by the same corporate legal teams that drafted the employment contracts making non-compliance economically fatal. Presented in neural-feed format with deliberate restraint — the immersive medium used to document the history of immersive technology.
cultural_impact: Became required reading in several Meridian Academic Consortium ethics programs before corporate curriculum review boards pressured its removal in 2209, by which point it had already shaped a generation of bioethicists and medical practitioners.
story_hooks: A character tracking down 'The Seventeen Minutes' discovers it documents a specific neurological condition — one that matches symptoms they or someone close to them has been experiencing.
One of the documentary's archival sources was a sealed corporate medical study; someone inside the corporation helped leak it and has never been identified.
A BCI technician who appears briefly in the film as a young interview subject is now a senior executive at a major augmentation firm and has been quietly trying to buy up all licensed copies.
